payload.title: judgment_funnel._tier0_verdict calls tier0_gate with contract None, so the falsifiability refusal and the per-family observable checks never run even when funnel_enabled is true, and only path and line existence at the sha is checked
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judgment_funnel.py:541-543 (the same loop resolves the rule contract a few lines later for the cache key, so it is available)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/tier0.py:240-249 (claim_not_falsifiable needs a non-None contract; with None nothing is refused)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/tier0.py:324-340 (the observable-driven premise checks read contract.observable, which is None)
aria-kernel/tests/test_tier0_gate.py:113-115 (a test pins 'no contract is a pass' as the whole law)
aria-kernel/tests/test_judgment_funnel.py:360-368 (the funnel test passes a plain item and asserts it reaches the fan-out; nothing asserts the contract reaches tier-0)
payload.rule_violated: WP-J operator protocol step 1 (ARIA-HIGH-675/677): a claim without a predicted observable or recipe is refused by name before any paid seat, and tier-0 is the one place that refuses it.
payload.notes: With funnel_enabled switched on, a finding of a rule that declares neither observable nor recipe passes tier-0, is routed and paid for although tier0_gate would return claim_not_falsifiable with the contract; lint '*' and doc-staleness findings are never put through their cited_line_bytes_at_sha or referenced_path_absent_at_sha checks. Latent while funnel_enabled is false (the shipped default). Close condition: Resolve the item's RuleContract with rule_contract.resolve_rule_contract inside _tier0_verdict and pass it to tier0_gate, leaving the fan-out's rule_contract_undeclared refusal as the owner of the undeclared case. Test: with funnel_enabled true, route_judgment_sample refuses an item whose rule has neither observable nor recipe as claim_not_falsifiable, and an item whose referenced path exists at the sha as tier0_observable_premise_violated (red today). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
